text:
Maya Chen: Repro: after PR #3427 (kernel-selector: hotswap fallback) we see 12-18% p95 tail increase on long-seq workloads. Attaching nsys timeline: https://perf.internal/nsys/2145678901

Arjun Patel: Thanks. Is this only on the kv-batcher path or everywhere?

Maya Chen: Mostly on requests that hit KV cache + batcher > 512 tokens. Short requests look fine. The kernel timeline shows extra small kernels firing between attention and matmul.

Tasha Lopez: Can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll run it locally.

Maya Chen: Sure — command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,cudnn --sample=none -o nsys_run  
  --force-overwrite --capture-range=cpu 0 --capture-range-end=cpu 200 \n  python -m benches.kv_long --model=mistral-7b --seq=1024 --batch=4
```
I recorded two runs: before PR (branch main@sha:ab12c3) and after PR (pr/3427@sha:ef45d6).

Samir Rao: I grabbed the two timelines and compared kernels. Looks like an extra kernel called small_matmul_kernel_v2 gets inserted ~5 times per request. Each occurrence is ~180us. That matches the delta.

Arjun Patel: small_matmul_kernel_v2 — that's the fallback path when selector fails to match optimized matmul, right? Could be selector heuristics misclassifying due to changed shape rounding.

Maya Chen: Exactly. The selector was changed to prefer tiling variant A for sequences > 256, but it seems for sequences near powers-of-two the fallback kicks in.

perf-bot: Automated perf-test failed for pr/3427 — latency p95 increased 14.2% on kv_long_seq job. See CI: https://ci.internal/runs/3427

Tasha Lopez: I ran nvprof to capture kernel names quickly (lighter than nsys):
```
nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace -o nv_out pr_run python -m benches.kv_long --seq=1024
nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace -o nv_out_base main_run python -m benches.kv_long --seq=1024
```
Diff shows small_matmul_kernel_v2 only present in pr_run.

Samir Rao: Let's bisect between ab12c3..ef45d6 to be sure. I can start a git-bisect with the perf harness. Plan:
```
git checkout ef45d6
git bisect start
# mark bad = ef45d6, good = ab12c3
git bisect bad ef45d6
git bisect good ab12c3
# run the perf script that runs the long seq benchmark and exits non-zero if p95 delta > 6%
./tools/perf_bisect.sh --job kv_long_seq --threshold 0.06
```
I'll leave it running on the bisect runner.

Maya Chen: Great. Also capturing perfetto to get the full CPU/GPU correlation:
```
python -m perfetto.recorder --out perfetto_pr.pb --duration 20 --cmd 'python -m benches.kv_long --seq=1024 --batch=4'
# open in perfetto UI and look at GPU slice alignment around the extra kernels
```

Arjun Patel: If bisect points to kernel-selector change commit, we should add a shape-matching fuzz test to the selector and a regression test in CI that runs the long-seq profile and fails if small_matmul_kernel_v2 appears more than N times.

perf-bot: Bisect job queued on runner-07 (ETA ~18m).

(18 minutes later)

deploy-bot: Bisect run finished on runner-07: culprit commit = b9f8d2 (kernel-selector: rounding tweak for tile-id).

Samir Rao: Confirmed locally. Reverting the rounding tweak in kernel_selector_routing() removes the extra fallback kernels. I pushed a patch that keeps the heuristic but clamps by a heuristic threshold. PR: https://git.internal/r/3462

Maya Chen: Nice. Can we add a microbenchmark to force shapes at 256, 512, 1024 to avoid regressions?

Arjun Patel: Yup — I'll add kv_long_seq variants and a selector unit test that asserts chosen kernel name for given dims. Also add a CI perf check that runs the nvprof smoke and greps for small_matmul_kernel_v2.

Tasha Lopez: I validated patched PR on perf cluster — p95 regressed back to within 1.5% of baseline. nvprof no longer shows small_matmul_kernel_v2.

Maya Chen: LGTM. Assigning postmortem: Samir write a short blameless writeup with nsys screenshots and root cause. Arjun add tests and CI hooks. Tasha will add perfetto traces to the incident artifacts.

Samir Rao: Will do, I'll upload the before/after nsys traces and the perfetto pb to the incident folder.

Maya Chen: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
